html:
A smallpox epidemic that swept Japan from 735 to 737 and killed roughly a third of the population, perhaps a million people. It was one of the worst disasters in the history of Nara Japan.

The disease entered through northern Kyushu, the gateway for ships from Korea and China, and spread along the roads to the capital at Nara. In 737 it killed all four Fujiwara brothers who led the government.

Its effects reached far:

  • Emperor Shōmu ordered temples built in every province and paid for the giant bronze Great Buddha of Tōdai-ji, to win the protection of Buddhism.
  • With so many farmers dead, fields went wild. In 743 the court let people keep new land they cleared forever, which undid the state land system of the Taihō Code and helped great private estates grow.

Smallpox returned to Japan again and again in later centuries.
sum: A smallpox epidemic that swept Japan from 735 to 737 and killed roughly a third of the population, perhaps a million people. It was one of the worst disasters in the history of Nara Japan.
